text:
Indeed, what does God do with that sea of curses
that rises every day toward his seraphim?
Like a despot sated with food and wine,
he falls asleep to the sweet sound of our blasphemies.

The lamentations of martyrs and the tortured
are surely an intoxicating symphony,
since, despite the blood their delight costs,
the heavens still do not seem sated!

Remember, Jesus, that Garden of Olives!
In utter simplicity you prayed on your knees
to him who, in his heaven, laughed at the nails
base executioners drove into your flesh,

When you saw the rabble of guardroom and kitchen
spit upon your divinity,
and when you felt the thorns pierce
your head where humankind had dwelt,

When the dreadful weight of your broken body
stretched your straining arms, and your blood
and sweat ran down your pale brow,
when you were displayed as a target before all,

Did you remember the brilliant, lovely days
when you came to fulfill the eternal promise,
when astride a gentle she-ass you traveled
roads strewn with flowers and branches,

When, your breast swollen with hope and courage,
you forcefully scourged the vile merchants,
when you were master? Did repentance not pierce
your side more deeply than the spear?

As for me, I shall surely leave satisfied
a world where action is no sister to the dream;
may I kill by the sword and die by the sword!
Saint Peter denied Jesus… he did well!

translation.title: The Denial of Saint Peter
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The poem’s blasphemous challenge and final endorsement of Peter’s denial are preserved.
